touches.subject: Spanish-language intake
touches.body:
Your site runs a Spanish version, so Spanish-speaking clients are finding you. The work behind that — records requests, follow-ups, status calls in both languages — is usually the part that strains first.

We place dedicated remote legal staff with PI firms, bilingual where it matters. One person, assigned to your cases, working in your systems — not a pooled service desk.

Worth a short call, or should I put it in writing first?

touches.skipped_reason: Skipped: the proof isn't a job posting, so there's no role to follow up on.

touches.subject: the unbilled hours
touches.body:
On contingency, every hour your team spends chasing records is unbilled, and it sits between you and the fee.

A demand writer isn't a cost saving. It shortens the gap to settlement — which is a different thing entirely, and the reason PI firms are usually the easiest version of this conversation.

Happy to walk through the numbers on a call.

touches.subject: a firm about your size
touches.body:
A six-attorney PI firm we work with had the same shape of problem: ad spend bringing in cases faster than two paralegals could process them.

They started with one demand writer. Their paralegals stopped doing records entirely and went back to actual case work.

Not saying that's you — but the pattern is common enough to mention.

touches.subject: the part people ask about
touches.body:
The question I usually get around now is about client information.

Straight answer: your person works inside your case management system under permissions you set, same as an in-house hire. NDA and confidentiality agreement signed before day one. You supervise the work the way you'd supervise anyone's.

Happy to send the agreement over to read before we ever speak.

touches.subject: maybe the wrong end
touches.body:
It's possible I've been aiming at the wrong end of this.

If the bottleneck isn't the demand side but the front — requests going out, chasing providers, the clinic that never responds — that's a document collector, and it's a smaller thing to start with.

Which end hurts more?

touches.subject: right person?
touches.body:
I may be writing to the wrong person entirely.

If someone else handles hiring and case workflow — office manager, firm administrator — I'm happy to talk to them instead and leave you out of it.

Otherwise I'll assume the timing isn't right.

touches.skipped_reason: Skipped: there's no open posting to ask about.

touches.subject: closing the loop
touches.body:
I'll stop here.

If the records backlog becomes a bigger problem later, we're easy to find. No hard feelings either way.
